source: OECD, India: Estimates of Support to Agriculture (PSE/CSE cookbook, 2024), B.1 Based on variable input use: besides the fertiliser subsidy and MISS (listed in pse_input_items_2022.csv) the B1 payments are the Electricity Subsidy (unit cost of power supply less the average agricultural tariff, times the supplies to agriculture; CEA data, 2020-22 a three-year moving average), the Irrigation Subsidy (states' revenue expenditure on irrigation less irrigation receipts; RBI State Finances), crop insurance premium subsidies, RKVY and small seed programmes. OECD Agricultural Policy Monitoring and Evaluation 2023 (India) and India's 2022-23 WTO input-subsidy notification describe the input subsidies as mainly fertiliser, electricity and irrigation water.
basis: Round-3 final QA item 9: India's PSE input support (OECD MONEVA PIV + PIS, 51.9 bn) less the listed fertiliser and credit items was one rate (-14 percent) on every crp input, services included. GTAP 12 ch.11A (Figure 11.1) maps PSE B1 to input subsidies on the inputs they pay for; the OECD amounts by B1 item are not in data/oecd_pse (MONEVA gives PIV as one total). The remainder is put on the rows of the two large B1 items whose amounts are not sourced, electricity (ely) and irrigation water (wat), split by the crp column's basic purchases of the two rows (one support rate on both). It includes the small B1 items (crop insurance, RKVY, seeds) and the on-farm services PIS (0.07 bn). NEEDS-SOURCE: the OECD India PSE country file with the B1 amounts by item (electricity, irrigation, insurance) would split the remainder by item. The IEA electricity consumption subsidy (B15, S13 fuel_subsidies) is also on India's ely row for every buyer; the farm part of it overlaps the OECD electricity item (reported, not netted).
